the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing

than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison

bell: a hollow metal device that rings when struck

required: A valid passport is required for international travel.
other: different from the one already mentioned; additional

surrounding: Smoke from the fire drifted over the surrounding countryside for days.

attention: notice, thought or interest given to something

smaller: less large in size, amount, or degree, compared with something else
This car is smaller than the one we had before.
headlines: titles printed at the top of newspaper articles
Most readers only skim the headlines before scrolling on.
interesting: The museum's new exhibit is genuinely interesting for children and adults.
dismissal: the act of rejecting or removing something or someone
His dismissal from the company came as a complete shock.
context: the circumstances or setting in which something happens
Without more context, the quote could easily be misunderstood.
appears: becomes visible, or seems to be the case
The moon appears larger when it is near the horizon.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
feel: to sense or experience something physically or emotionally
You can feel the ground shake when a train passes by.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
without: not having; in the absence of
This arrangement lets the wheel turn into a lean without anyone touching the handlebars.
requiring: Tasks requiring careful judgement were left to senior staff.
misled: given a false or mistaken impression; deceived
Investors felt they had been misled about the company's true finances.
knowing: having information or understanding about something
Knowing when to stop working is an important skill for bakers.
even: used to emphasise something surprising or extreme
Your body keeps track of time even in a dark room.
never: at no time; not on any occasion
She had never travelled outside her home country before that trip.
becomes: The sky becomes darker earlier as autumn approaches.
prescription: a written instruction from a doctor for a medicine
The doctor wrote a prescription for antibiotics after examining her throat.
same: They wore the same colour shirts to the reunion.
surrounds: is or goes all around something
A low stone wall surrounds the entire garden and orchard.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception
Somebody must repaint the roof every few years.
ever: Nobody can write down rules that nobody ever actually knew.
question: /ˈkwestʃən/
n
a sentence asked to get information or express doubt
câu hỏi, vấn đề
Nobody could answer the teacher's difficult question about gravity.
query
inquiry
issue
raises: brings up a question or concern; increases something
The report raises serious concerns about the safety of the factory.
whether: used to express doubt or choice between alternatives
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but how it is done.
hand: the part of the body at the end of the arm, used for holding
She raised her hand to ask the teacher a question.
out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
sugar: a sweet substance used to flavour food and drink
She takes her coffee with no sugar at all.
how: She explained how the machine works in simple terms.
we: used to refer to the speaker and one or more other people
We forget most of what we just learned within a day.
credit: an arrangement to receive goods or money now and pay later
The shop owner extended credit to regular customers during hard times.
belonged: was the property of, or a proper part of, something
The farmland once belonged to a single family for three generations.
circumstances: the conditions or facts connected with an event or situation
Under different circumstances, the outcome might have been very different.
handed: gave or passed something to someone using the hand
The waiter handed her the menu with a polite smile.
